sources.title: Chinese exchanges ease margin trading requirements to aid stock markets
Libya’s eastern government suspects drone attack caused explosion on Russian ship

stories.headline: China’s exchanges announce minimum margin ratio cut to 80% from 100%, effective 30 November
stories.body: Reuters reported that China’s Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges announced a minimum margin-financing ratio reduction from 100% to 80%, effective 30 November 2026. Shanghai and Shenzhen also planned fee cuts, while Shenzhen proposed ChiNext market-making rules. Reuters cited outstanding margin loans of roughly CNY2.2tn versus a late-June CNY3tn peak. These are dated outstanding balances, not new lending or realised investment returns. The lower requirement permits greater borrowing to buy shares against equivalent collateral; implementation is still ahead. No attributable post-announcement share-price or FX response was verified.
stories.analysis: More financing capacity may support liquidity while increasing leverage and forced-selling risk.
stories.watch_next: 30 November implementation, margin balances, market breadth and volatility.

stories.topic: LIBYA / RUSSIA / MARITIME SECURITY / GEOPOLITICAL RISK
stories.headline: Libyan authorities suspect drone attack behind Russian vessel explosion at Benghazi
stories.body: Reuters reported that Libya’s eastern-based government cited preliminary findings pointing to a suspected drone attack on a Russian vessel at Benghazi naval base. Medical sources reported injuries and no known deaths; the number and nationalities of injured people were not established. No one had claimed responsibility and attribution remained unresolved. A later Reuters carrier said normal port operations had resumed, while an earlier copy described resumption as conditional on fire control; the exact restoration time is not established here. No verified wider commercial-shipping disruption or attributable oil, freight or bond-market movement was supplied.
stories.analysis: The incident raises maritime-security concerns without establishing responsibility or a broader commercial-supply interruption.
stories.watch_next: Official investigation, vessel damage, confirmed attribution and any operational restrictions.
